identity.title: Ability to stand and walk unaided (truncal ataxia grade; inability = central marker)

technique.how: Ask the patient to sit unsupported on the bed edge, then stand and walk a few metres unaided, then tandem walk if able. Grade truncal ataxia: 0 none; 1 mild imbalance walking; 2 cannot walk without support; 3 cannot stand or sit unsupported (falls to one side). Have an assistant close by.
technique.prerequisites: Patient not sedated, hemodynamically stable, no acute orthopaedic injury; use a gait belt or two assistants for frail patients.
technique.contraindications: Unstable spine or fracture, severe hypotension, or inability to protect the patient from a fall.

interpretation.positive_finding: Inability to stand or sit unsupported (grade 3) or to walk unaided (grade 2) in acute vertigo strongly favours a central cause; grade 3 was seen only in central AVS in the HINTS cohort and grade 2-3 ataxia had 92% sensitivity for stroke vs vestibular neuritis.
interpretation.negative_finding: Walking unaided, even if veering, is typical of vestibular neuritis but does not exclude stroke; roughly two thirds of strokes in AVS lacked severe truncal ataxia.
interpretation.pitfalls: Intoxication, sedatives, Wernicke encephalopathy, and deconditioning in the elderly also impair standing; interpret in context and check glucose and thiamine risk. Truncal ataxia can occur without nystagmus in central vertigo, so absent nystagmus does not remove the need to test gait.
interpretation.changes_what: Cannot stand or walk unaided: manage as posterior-circulation stroke (MRI, stroke pathway) regardless of oculomotor findings. Walks unaided with peripheral HINTS: supports vestibular neuritis.

estimates.target_condition: Central AVS (stroke in AICA/PICA territory) vs vestibular neuritis
estimates.population: 52 prospectively studied patients with acute vestibular syndrome (central stroke or vestibular neuritis); finding = grade 2-3 truncal ataxia
estimates.computed_from: LRs computed from abstract sens 0.92 and spec 0.67: LR+ = 0.92/0.33 = 2.79; LR- = 0.08/0.67 = 0.12.
estimates.quote: ataxia to differentiate patients with vestibular neuritis from patients with stroke resulted in a 92% sensitivity (95% CI 79-100%), a 67% specificity (95% CI 47-86%)

estimates.target_condition: Ischemic stroke in acute vestibular syndrome; finding = severe truncal ataxia (cannot sit unassisted)
estimates.population: 101 consecutive AVS patients with >=1 stroke risk factor (69 ischemic strokes, 25 peripheral)
estimates.reference_standard: MRI (DWI) or CT plus clinical follow-up
estimates.location: Table 4 (Bedside signs and initial MRI with DWI test properties for ischemic stroke in AVS), PMC4593511

sources.citation: Kattah JC, Martinez C, Zalazar G, Batuecas A, Lemos J, Carmona S. Role of incubitus truncal ataxia, and equivalent standing grade 3 ataxia in the diagnosis of central acute vestibular syndrome. J Neurol Sci. 2022;441:120374.

Kattah JC, Talkad AV, Wang DZ, Hsieh YH, Newman-Toker DE. HINTS to diagnose stroke in the acute vestibular syndrome: three-step bedside oculomotor examination more sensitive than early MRI diffusion-weighted imaging. Stroke. 2009;40(11):3504-3510.
Carmona S, Martinez C, Zalazar G, Koohi N, Kaski D. Acute truncal ataxia without nystagmus in patients with acute vertigo. Eur J Neurol. 2023;30(6):1785-1790.

Tarnutzer AA, Berkowitz AL, Robinson KA, Hsieh YH, Newman-Toker DE. Does my dizzy patient have a stroke? A systematic review of bedside diagnosis in acute vestibular syndrome. CMAJ. 2011;183(9):E571-E592.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not attempt unsupervised in frail, hypotensive, or sedated patients; do not attribute inability to stand to intoxication or age without excluding stroke.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: A dizzy patient who cannot stand or sit unsupported has a central lesion until MRI proves otherwise; CT is insufficient for the posterior fossa.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Grading is semi-quantitative and examiner-dependent; the 2022 study found inability to sit still correlated well with formal truncal ataxia grade and can substitute when standing is unsafe.

extraction_notes: Primary numbers from the Kattah 2022 abstract (grade 2-3 ataxia, n=52; prevalence of stroke not stated in abstract so left null; LRs computed) and from Kattah 2009 Table 4 in PMC full text (severe truncal ataxia = cannot sit unassisted; Table 1 gives the same finding at 0% peripheral vs 34% central with NLR 0.66). Carmona 2023 (15% of acute vertigo had truncal ataxia without nystagmus) cited as context, not an accuracy estimate. Tarnutzer 2011 pooled gait data not accessible (PMC abstract-only).
